correctness.rationale: For n≥3 the rotation representation forces zero mean and scalar covariance. The farthest-center constraint along a ray reduces to r²+2atr+a²≤1 with t the maximum antipodal dot product. Implicit differentiation gives ∂t log r=−a/d; differentiating this in a gives −1/d³ since d²=1−a²(1−t²). Put q=r² and tilt angular measure by q/Eq. The logarithmic derivative of E(q²)/(Eq)² is 2 Cov(q,∂a log q)/E(q) under the tilted measure. Both functions decrease strictly in t for a>0 and t is nonconstant under a positive density, so the independent-copy covariance identity is strictly positive. The disk value follows by continuity; r/(1−a)→1/t uniformly because t≥cos(π/n)>0. The polygon sector integral of sec⁴ has primitive tan φ+tan³φ/3, confirming the stated upper constant. The arc flux at half-angle β is 1−a cos u, and its product with 1+a²−2a cos u integrates to the stated J; differentiating the proposed antiderivative in β and checking its zero constant also gives the identity. At a=0 the nominal arcs simply partition the disk. The exact algebra replay is `python3 /workspace/checks/independent_01_05.py` (check 1). The frozen 151-assertion run is author-reported corroboration, not an independent rerun or proof of the continuum statement.
